title: Break and continue
recap: A continue statement jumps to the next iteration of the enclosing loop, skipping the rest of the body. A break statement exits the loop entirely.
Together they let a loop filter and stop without nesting extra conditions. Both work in while, do while, for, and switch statements.
objectives: Implement sumCheckpoints from its behavioral contract.
Practice the lesson construct by writing the control flow yourself.
Handle multiple inputs and edge cases without hard-coded example answers.
warnings: The examples are not the whole test suite; implement the general behavior.
Do not edit the test drivers. Only the supplied public function signatures are fixed.
Console output and exact source tokens are not graded.
challenge: Implement sumCheckpoints. Visit values 1 through limit in order. Stop BEFORE processing a value equal to stopAt, even if it is a multiple of 3. Skip multiples of 3. Sum all other visited values. Use break for the stop and continue for the skip. If limit <= 0 return 0; if stopAt is outside [1, limit], scan the entire range. Limits are at most 1000.
hints: Check the stop condition before the multiple-of-three condition.
Use continue to bypass accumulation for a skipped value.
Return the accumulated total after the loop.
